title: Check your own digital footprint
scenario: You want to see what the internet shows about your own name, handle or small brand so you can clean up old or risky information.
steps: List only your own names, handles and brand terms
Ask the AI for a checklist of public places to search and what to look for
Note what to remove or lock down, then update privacy settings
safety_note: Search only your own footprint or a brand you officially manage, never another person, because that can become stalking or doxxing. Do not paste your phone number, address or ID numbers into the AI; describe them in general words.

title: Spot a phishing email
scenario: A suspicious email asks you to update KYC or reset a password, and you want help deciding if it is phishing.
steps: Copy the email text and headers with your own address and names replaced by placeholders
Ask the AI to list red flags such as sender mismatch, urgency and odd links
Report the mail to your IT team or the platform and delete it without clicking
safety_note: Never click links or open attachments to test them, and do not paste live links into tools you do not trust. Redact PII, card numbers, OTPs, client names and internal IPs before pasting anything into an AI tool.

title: Turn a news story into a scam awareness Reel
scenario: You read a news report about a new scam and want a short Hinglish Reel script that warns your followers.
steps: Paste a short summary of the news in your own words
Ask the AI for a 30 second script with a hook, how the scam works and how to stay safe
Add 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in at the end and check every fact against the original report
safety_note: Explain how to stay safe, not how to run the scam, and do not name accused people in ongoing cases. Blur any victim details, phone numbers or screenshots that show personal data.

title: Draft a complaint for cybercrime.gov.in
scenario: You or a family member lost money or faced harassment online and want a clear, factual complaint draft before filing.
steps: Write down the dates, amounts, platforms and what happened in simple points
Ask the AI to arrange these facts into a clear complaint using only what you gave it
Call 1930 quickly for money fraud, file on cybercrime.gov.in, and consult a lawyer if needed
safety_note: Use the AI only to organise your own facts; it should not invent details or give legal advice. Keep full account numbers, card numbers and OTPs out of the AI and add them only on the official portal.

title: Draft a basic security policy
scenario: Your small team needs a simple password and device use policy written in plain language.
steps: Describe your team size, tools and current practices in general terms
Ask the AI for a short draft policy with clear do and do not points
Review it with your team and a qualified advisor before adopting it
safety_note: Treat the AI draft as a starting point, not a final legal or compliance document. Do not share real passwords, network diagrams, internal IPs or client names while drafting.

title: DPDP readiness check for a small business
scenario: You run a small shop or startup that collects customer names and phone numbers and want to know what to look at under the DPDP Act 2023.
steps: List what personal data you collect, why, and where it is stored, without real customer records
Ask the AI for a general readiness checklist covering notice, consent, security and deletion
Confirm the points and any timelines with a lawyer or the official DPDP Act and Rules text
safety_note: The AI gives general awareness only, and any deadline or penalty it mentions must be checked against official sources. Never paste real customer lists, phone numbers or payment data into the tool.

title: Prepare for a SOC analyst interview
scenario: You have a SOC analyst interview coming up and want practice questions with feedback on your answers.
steps: Share the job description and your experience level
Ask the AI for common SOC questions and answer them one by one
Ask for feedback and then revise weak answers using official vendor docs and your own lab notes
safety_note: Practise with labs you own or legal training platforms, never live systems without written permission. Do not paste past employer logs, client names or internal IPs as examples.

title: Plan a college cyber awareness session
scenario: You are invited to give a one hour cyber safety talk at a college and need a structure that students will enjoy.
steps: Tell the AI the audience, duration and topics like UPI fraud, sextortion and safe social media
Ask for an outline with short stories, a quiz and key takeaways
Add helpline 1930, cybercrime.gov.in and a reminder to talk to a trusted adult or lawyer
safety_note: Teach defence only and avoid live demos of hacking tools or real accounts. Use made up examples instead of real victim stories, names or screenshots.

title: Triage security logs
scenario: You have a batch of firewall or login logs showing unusual activity and want help spotting patterns worth investigating.
steps: Mask usernames, internal IPs, hostnames and client names with placeholders
Paste a small sample and ask the AI to group events and flag likely suspicious patterns
Confirm every finding in your SIEM or original logs before escalating
safety_note: Work only on logs from systems you are authorised to monitor, and follow your organisation's data handling policy. Redact PII, card numbers, OTPs, client names and internal IPs before pasting anything into an AI tool.

title: Summarise a vulnerability scan report
scenario: You ran an authorised vulnerability scan on your own or a client's systems with written permission and need a clear summary for management.
steps: Remove client names, internal IPs, hostnames and any credentials from the report
Ask the AI to group findings by severity and explain business impact in simple words
Check each item against the scanner output and vendor advisories before sharing the summary
safety_note: Never scan or test systems you do not own or lack written permission for. Ask the AI only for fixes and priorities, not exploit steps, and keep raw reports out of public tools.

title: Build an incident timeline
scenario: After a security incident you have notes, alerts and emails scattered everywhere and need one clean timeline for the report.
steps: Collect events with time, source and a short description, using placeholders for people and systems
Ask the AI to sort them into a timeline and point out gaps or conflicting times
Verify each entry against original evidence and keep the evidence untouched for any legal process
safety_note: The AI only arranges facts you supply, so mark anything it suggests as unconfirmed until checked. Redact PII, client names, internal IPs and any credentials, and follow your incident response and legal team's guidance.

title: Explain a CVE for your team
scenario: A new CVE affects software your organisation uses and you need a short internal advisory that both engineers and managers understand.
steps: Paste the CVE ID, the official advisory text and the affected product versions
Ask the AI to explain the risk, who is affected and the recommended patch or workaround in plain words
Check the details against the vendor advisory and NVD or CERT-In before sending it out
safety_note: Focus on detection, patching and mitigation, not on writing or running exploits. Do not paste your asset inventory, internal IPs or client names; describe affected systems in general terms.
